name: NATS
description: Protects against destructive NATS/JetStream operations like deleting streams, consumers, \ key-value entries, objects, and accounts.

destructive_patterns.name: nats-stream-delete
destructive_patterns.description: nats stream delete/rm removes a JetStream stream and all its messages.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a JetStream stream permanently removes all stored messages, \ consumers, and configuration. Applications relying on this stream will \ lose access to historical data.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - nats stream info: Review stream details first \ - nats stream purge: Remove messages but keep the stream \ - Back up stream configuration before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: nats-stream-purge
destructive_patterns.description: nats stream purge deletes ALL messages from the stream.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Purging a stream removes all messages while keeping the stream and \ consumer configurations intact. Consumers will have no messages to \ process until new ones arrive.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - nats stream info: Check message count first \ - Use --seq to purge only messages up to a specific sequence \ - Use --keep to retain the last N messages

destructive_patterns.name: nats-consumer-delete
destructive_patterns.description: nats consumer delete/rm removes a JetStream consumer.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a consumer removes its acknowledgment state and delivery \ tracking. Messages may be redelivered to other consumers or lost \ if this was the only consumer.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - nats consumer info: Review consumer state first \ - Pause the consumer instead of deleting \ - Ensure other consumers exist for critical streams

destructive_patterns.name: nats-kv-delete
destructive_patterns.description: nats kv del/rm deletes key-value entries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting KV entries removes data that applications may depend on. \ If history is disabled, the deletion is permanent and cannot be \ recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - nats kv get: Retrieve and back up the value first \ - nats kv history: Check if history is enabled \ - Use TTL for automatic expiration instead of manual deletion

destructive_patterns.name: nats-object-delete
destructive_patterns.description: nats object delete removes an object from the store.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an object from the object store removes the file and its \ metadata. Applications expecting this object will receive errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - nats object info: Review object details first \ - Download the object before deletion \ - Use object versioning if available

destructive_patterns.name: nats-account-delete
destructive_patterns.description: nats account delete removes an account and its resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a NATS account removes all streams, consumers, and permissions \ associated with that account. All applications using this account will \ lose connectivity.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review account resources before deletion \ - Migrate resources to another account first \ - Disable the account instead of deleting
